title: Redwood PLG Quickstart discovery - Phoenix Data
summary: Intro discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Customer focused on quicktime-to-first-token, free credits for eval, and deciding hosted vs dedicated later. Security (SOC2, VPC) flagged by security lead. Agreed next step: send quickstart link, pricing tiers, and schedule a short hands-on demo with SE to provision tokens and run basic latency tests.
next_steps: Redwood: send quickstart guide + free credits link (Derek)
Redwood: schedule 30m demo to walk through getting first token & sample calls (Sana)
Customer: confirm pilot scope & proposed timelines (Maya)
Customer: share list of security questions / SOC2 contact (Liam)
action_items: Derek Chen - send quickstart + free credits link - due 2026-03-06
Sana Iqbal - schedule 30m hands-on demo and sample benchmark spreadsheet - due 2026-03-07
Maya Patel - share pilot success criteria and internal stakeholders - due 2026-03-09

transcript: 00:00 Derek (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, im Derek, i'm the AE working with Phoenix Data. quick agenda - 1) learn about your use case 2) show how quick the PLG quickstart is 3) next steps. 00:12 Maya (Head of ML): thanks, yeah we just want a short call, our team is exploring hosted APIs first, want to see time to first token and cost. 00:25 Tom (Eng Manager): we run everything on aws, mostly on EKS, some GCP for data analytics. latency is important for front-end features, cost matters for batch embed jobs. 00:40 Sana (Redwood SE): hi all, im Sana, i run demos and benchmarks. quick question - are you evaluating open models only or closed ones too? 00:50 Maya: mostly open models, cost/latency tradeoffs, but we'll consider hosted solutions if the SLA and security look good. 01:05 Liam (Security): quick intro, im Liam, security lead, i'll be looking at SOC2 evidence, data retention, KMS options and VPC/private deployment path. 01:17 Derek: perfect, that's helpful. on PLG quickstart we provide free credits for teams to get to first token in under 10 minutes typically. you can sign up self-serve, get API key, and run sample requests. 01:33 Maya: under 10 minutes? that sounds great, can you walk through the exact steps? 01:38 Sana: sure — step 1 sign up at console.redwood.ai, step 2 create an API key, step 3 call the REST endpoint with a sample prompt. we also have SDKs (python/node) and curl examples. in practice most teams hit their first token in < 15 minutes, sometimes 5-10. 01:54 Tom: any IP or data residency issues with the hosted API? we process PII in some pipelines. 02:01 Derek: good call — hosted is multi-tenant but we offer data retention controls and opt-out for data training; for stricter needs we have Dedicated or Private options where you get reserved capacity or a VPC/private control plane. 02:14 Liam: for SOC2/ISO we need audit logs and KMS/HSM integration — is that available with hosted? 02:22 Sana: audit logs and RBAC are part of the Console; KMS integration and customer-managed keys are supported on Dedicated and Private. we can share SOC2 docs and our security whitepaper. 02:35 Maya: what's the typical path — start hosted and then move to Dedicated? 02:40 Derek: that's common — start with PLG/self-serve to validate dev velocity and get usage patterns, then move to Dedicated when you need guaranteed throughput, isolated capacity, or stricter controls. 02:52 Tom: any cold-start latency differences between hosted and dedicated? 02:55 Sana: dedicated gives more consistent latency due to reserved GPU pools, hosted is optimized but can have variance at peak. we also do smart routing and fallback to compatible variants to keep requests online. 03:10 Maya: pricing model for the PLG quickstart — is it per token? and how do free credits apply? 03:17 Derek: hosted is usage-based (per token/embedding unit). free credits are issued to new accounts for X dollars of usage to run experiments; they don't expire quickly and you can run proof-of-concept calls. we'll send the exact promo link. 03:30 Tom: can we run a small benchmark during the demo — e.g., 100 requests measuring p95 latency and token cost? 03:36 Sana: yes we can run a small benchmark live and share a spreadsheet with cost breakdown per model. 03:43 Liam: curious about model catalog — do you host community models or curated ones only? 03:48 Sana: catalog includes curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles; we expose model variants and quantized options with performance notes. 03:58 Maya: great. for pilot timeline we want 2-4 weeks to validate latency and quality, then an expanded pilot if metrics look good. 04:06 Derek: sounds reasonable. typical next step is 1) send quickstart + credits 2) schedule 30m hands-on demo to get your engineers the API key and run the benchmark 3) security sends SOC2 questions and we reply. 04:20 Tom: what's the onboarding friction for developers? any SDKs or infra changes? 04:25 Sana: usually low — just install the SDK or call REST. for on-prem or VPC you'd have more infra work, but for self-serve hosted it's just API keys. 04:36 Maya: any rate limits on free credits / trial? 04:40 Derek: trials have soft rate limits to prevent abuse but they are higher than typical dev usage; we can bump for a short pilot if needed. 04:50 Liam: about logs and audit - can we get full request/response logs for a pilot? we may need redaction options. 04:57 Sana: yes, we provide request-level logging in the Console and you can configure retention and redaction patterns; full export is available on Dedicated/Private. 05:08 Maya: ok i'm interested. can you also share a short checklist for the SE-led demo so we can invite the right folks? 05:14 Derek: absolutely — we'll send a suggested checklist (engineer + security rep + product owner). 05:20 Tom: timeline — we can do the demo next week, maybe Wednesday. 05:24 Sana: i'll follow up with availability. 05:28 Maya: thanks, final Q — do you support function/tool calling or streaming for chat use cases? 05:33 Sana: yes, streaming responses and function calling are supported, and we can show examples in the demo. 05:40 Derek: recap — Derek send quickstart + free credits link, Sana schedule demo and bring bench spreadsheet, Liam to send security questions. any other blockers? 05:51 Maya: none from me, thanks. 05:54 Tom: none. 05:56 Liam: no. 05:58 Derek: great, we'll follow up. thanks everyone. 06:01 call ended
